Based on Table 2, the passive-targeting delivery systems with a particle size of 150 nm or more are:

* LNP | – | si-FOXM1 | FOXM1 | 90–100 nm (does not meet the condition)
* Polymer | mPEG5K- | siSLITRK4 | SLITRK4 | ~141 nm (meets the condition)
* PLGA/PLA/ | KRAS siRNA TGF-β | KRAS TGF-β | ~180 nm (meets the condition)
* sEVs | – | VEGFR2 siRNA mTOR | VEGFR2 | ~150 nm (meets the condition)
* MOF@EVs | – | siTEAD4 | TEAD4 | ~168 nm (meets the condition)
* Exosome | – | DARS-AS1 siRNA | DARS-AS1 | 78.82 ±11.85 nm (does not meet the condition)
* AuNP | PEG-SH | TUBB2B siRNA- AuNP | TUBB2B | – (does not meet the condition, as the particle size is not specified)
* SPIONs | PEN | siSnail2 | Snail2 | ~60 nm (does not meet the condition)
* MOF | – | DDP | VEGF | ~485 nm (meets the condition, and is the largest)

Therefore, the largest passive-targeting delivery system is MOF | – | DDP | VEGF | ~485 nm.

question: In Table 2, which passive-targeting delivery systems have a particle size of 150 nm or more, and which of them is the largest?
